functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the muscle with this origin: Supraspinous fossa. Action: Initiates abduction of the arm.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Supraspinatus: Initiates abduction of the arm. Nerve: Suprascapular nerve (C4, C5, C6).

functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the muscle with this origin: Infraspinous fossa. Action: Lateral rotation of the arm.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Infraspinatus: Lateral rotation of the arm. Nerve: Suprascapular nerve (C4, C5, C6).

functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the muscle with this origin: Coracoid process. Action: Flexion and adduction of the arm.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Coracobrachialis: Flexion and adduction of the arm. Nerve: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5, C6, C7).

functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the muscle with this origin: Transverse processes of C1–C4. Action: Elevation of the scapula.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Levator scapulae: Elevation of the scapula. Nerve: Dorsal scapular nerve (C4, C5), as listed in this lecture.

functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the muscle with this origin: Upper eight ribs. Action: Protraction and rotation of scapula; holds scapula against chest wall.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Serratus anterior: Protraction and rotation of scapula; holds scapula against chest wall. Nerve: Long thoracic nerve (C5, C6, C7).

functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the muscle with this origin: Ribs 3, 4 and 5. Action: Scapular protraction, shoulder depression and elevation of ribs.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Pectoralis minor: Scapular protraction, shoulder depression and elevation of ribs. Nerve: Medial pectoral nerve (C6, C7, C8), as listed in this lecture.

functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the muscle with this origin: T7–T12 spines, lumbar fascia, iliac crest, inferior three or four ribs and inferior scapular angle. Action: Extension, adduction and medial rotation of arm.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Latissimus dorsi: Extension, adduction and medial rotation of arm. Nerve: Thoracodorsal nerve (C6, C7, C8).

functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the muscle with this origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus. Action: Flexion of forearm in mid-pronation.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Brachioradialis: Flexion of forearm in mid-pronation. Nerve: Radial nerve.
